hypothesis: A small number of independent winners supplied most of the net profit and the nine-slot account rejected many simultaneous eligible contracts. Within the same available capital, distributing an oversubscribed batch across more contracts may catch more long tails.
only_change: Represent the same nine full-size reservations as eighteen half-size lots. At each original 12H clock first remove contracts with an existing funded position. Let F be free half lots (a lot releases only after the runner's exit hour) and N the count of eligible new symbols. If 2N<=F give each two lots. Otherwise admit min(N,F) contracts in frozen low-prior-ATR priority, giving them one lot each, then give leftover lots up to a second lot in the same priority. Never reserve >18 half lots or open multiple economic positions on one symbol. No cash transfer or reallocation of already funded positions.
mechanics: Each half lot uses the existing native two-thirds 2R partial / one-third EMA runner and VectorBT shared cash sizing. Identical simultaneous lots of one contract are grouped into one economic trade for cash payoff and win rate. Native 5bp market / 2bp maker, no funding/impact. The policy cannot look at a current batch's future results or at the final set of winners.
validation: Control run gives either two half lots or none to each new contract; verify its original funded identities, equity and PnL against the frozen nine-slot account before evaluating. Run same-policy OKX and Binance full native periods. If development passes (100 trades, win>=30%, cash/return payoff>=2.5, DD upper<=35%) run later same-parent controls and 5bp adverse slippage. Do not rank by later returns. Past data were already researched.
